Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple, well-defined pulmonary nodules of varying sizes (some approaching 3 cm) that are predominantly located in the lower lung zones without obvious calcification. This specific radiographic pattern—multiple bilateral nodules with a tendency toward the lower lobes and potential cavitation/necrosis—is characteristic of necrotizing sarcoid granulomatosis, distinguishing it from the upper-zone predominance of tuberculosis or the uniform distribution of classic sarcoidosis.
